findings.reason: The searches reproduce the absence of a named Markoff target in the short roadmap/stage texts and of a Markoff API in the pinned libraries, but that does not establish the claimed absence of an owner. PROTOCOL.md section 16 explicitly assigns missing mathematics inside an existing proposed layer through an accepted source route; it adds that paper to the blueprint instructions and does not require a simultaneous edit to the older roadmap description or library audit. At the reviewed commit, PAPER-MARTIN-25 route 1 assigns items /1–/13 (equation, Vieta maps, positivity, descent, tree, reduction) to CA.4, and its review accepts that ownership. PAPER-GHOSH-SARNAK-22 route 1 adds the level surfaces and descent, PAPER-CHEN-24 route 1 adds the normalization comparison, and PAPER-GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19 route 1 assigns /1–/5, including the n-variable equation, exceptional families and descent, to the same owner; each route is independently accepted. Read those current result/review files under https://github.com/CBirkbeck/tauceti-explorer/blob/e483a30e545b0d5c5ea3ef5e8aacaebdb5289564/research/blueprint/papers/ . The live blueprint issue #1025 already includes the Martin source and all thirteen item IDs under its mandatory added sources. The remaining accepted routes are inputs to the same mechanism: make_queue.py accepted_routes at lines 388–401, source-route collection at 834–838, and added_sources at 485–490. Its latest issue-body snapshot predates some additions, which is a queue/publication timing distinction, not evidence of ownerless mathematics. Source checks: Martin §1 (published p.623, arXiv:2502.15960 p.1); Ghosh–Sarnak arXiv:1706.06712v3 §§1–2; Chen arXiv:2011.12940v2 §5.5 pp.80–81; Gamburd–Magee–Ronan arXiv:1603.06267v3 (1.1), Definition 15, Proposition 16 and Corollary 17. The theory is substantive, but the accepted routes already contain the proposed additions. Preserve one CA.4 carrier and import it in downstream designs; no new ownership or mandatory target-creation fix follows from this finding.

The trace problem differs from Mahler-measure lower bounds, but it is already expressly assigned to CA.6 by accepted PAPER-SMITH-24 route 3: items /1–/3 define its classical objects and auxiliary-polynomial method, while /17 goes to CA.3. The independent review accepts route 3 precisely to make the new LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers roadmap import the constant rather than define it again. Under PROTOCOL.md section 16 this is an existing blueprint source obligation; omission from the earlier short layer description is not an uncovered mathematical target. Read the current result/review files at https://github.com/CBirkbeck/tauceti-explorer/blob/e483a30e545b0d5c5ea3ef5e8aacaebdb5289564/research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SMITH-24.result.json and PAPER-SMITH-24.review.json, alongside CA.6, its AUDIT-18 record and the accepted RS-03 scope. The proposed repair also gives a false definition: lambda_SSS is not the infimum of trace/degree over all non-rational totally positive algebraic integers. A root of X^2-3X+1 is a non-rational totally positive algebraic integer with ratio 3/2, already below the stated Schur lower bound exp(1/2). Smith arXiv:2111.12660v2, Notation 5.8 and Example 5.9, p.37, defines the relevant cofinite liminf; the finite-exception threshold must be the greatest one, not an ordinary infimum (the introduction's word “least”, reproduced in the extraction, is a misstatement exposed by p.37). Theorem 1.1, p.2, already disproves lambda_SSS=2 and is assigned to the new roadmap, so do not turn that historical expectation into a new conjectural endpoint. The suggested library reuse also needs a comparison: NumberField.IsTotallyPositive at https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/TotallyPositive.lean#L70 only tests real places and is vacuous in a totally complex ambient field. For the paper's all-conjugates-positive condition require integrality and real conjugates (for example work in the totally real field Q(alpha)), then reuse that predicate; Mathlib NumberField.IsTotallyReal at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/InfinitePlace/TotallyRealComplex.lean#L47 states the needed real-place condition. These mathematical cautions constrain the future blueprint; they do not establish the alleged owner/coverage omission or justify the proposed new target.
